query_text: Build a data scientist research portfolio app that feels like a personal archive rather than a generic resume site — the kind of thing that has its own quiet confidence and visual identity. For my phone, it should open to a clean list of research projects, each with a title, the key question it was trying to answer, and one standout chart or result image. Tapping into a project gives a short write-up with the tools used and what the work actually found. It should feel curated, not cluttered.

Need a mobile app for showcasing an urban planner's project work — something that feels substantial and considered, the kind of portfolio that actually communicates the scale and intent behind each project rather than just listing names. Each project entry should have a cover image, a short description of what problem the city was trying to solve, and the key outcome. The overall feel should be calm and authoritative, like something worth bookmarking.

Build a tattoo artist design gallery app for mobile that has real personality — dark, tactile, the kind of space where the art actually breathes. It should open to a full-screen grid of finished tattoo photos organized loosely by style, like traditional, fine line, blackwork, and when you tap one it opens a close-up view with a short note about the concept and placement. The feel of the app should match the craft — intentional, bold, and a little raw.

Build a voice actor demo reel app for mobile that feels as carefully composed as the work itself — not just a playlist dumped on a page, but something with real taste and presence. It should open with a short artist introduction and then list demo clips by category like commercial, character, narration, and animation, with each one tappable to play right there. The whole thing should feel warm and professional, the kind of first impression that actually sticks.

Build a makeup artist before-and-after showcase app for my phone that has the elegance the work deserves — not just a photo dump, but something that makes each transformation feel intentional and worth pausing on. Each entry should show the before and after photos side by side with a tap to reveal the look details like occasion, products, and technique. The app should feel like a polished editorial piece rather than a social media scroll.

Create a physical therapist client results app for mobile that carries the quiet credibility the profession deserves — something that feels grounded and human rather than clinical and cold. Each case entry should show the presenting issue, the treatment approach used, and the measurable improvement, ideally with a short note from the client. The home screen of the app should lead with the most compelling outcomes so visitors immediately understand what kind of results this practice actually delivers.

Need a mobile app for a digital marketing manager's case study showcase that feels sharp and curated — the kind of thing that earns trust in the first few seconds rather than burying the good stuff under corporate padding. Each case entry should lead with the challenge, then show the strategy in plain terms, and close with the results that actually mattered, like the numbers that moved. The app should have a confident, editorial feel that matches the work it's presenting.

A fine art curator gallery app for mobile that carries the weight and intentionality of the role — something that feels like walking into a thoughtfully arranged space rather than flipping through a generic portfolio. The app's home screen shows current and past exhibitions with a cover image and a short framing statement for each, and tapping into one reveals the featured works with the curator's notes on why they belong together. The whole thing should feel considered, not decorative.

Make a theater director production portfolio app for my phone that actually does justice to the work — something that feels like it understands what live performance is, not just a list of show titles. Each production should have a mood-setting photo, the venue and season, and a short director's statement about the artistic vision behind it. The home screen of the app should feel like an opening night program — composed, atmospheric, and proud of what it's showing.

Need a dog trainer results showcase app for mobile that has warmth and credibility in equal measure — something that feels like it was built by someone who genuinely loves what they do, not assembled from a template. Each entry should show the dog's story, what behavioral challenge they came in with, and what they achieved by the end of training, ideally with a before-and-after photo. The app should feel personal and specific, the kind of thing a potential client scrolls through and immediately trusts.

Make a real estate agent sales portfolio app for my phone that feels like the work of someone who actually cares about the details — not just a list of sold properties, but a showcase that tells the story of each deal. Each listing should have a great photo of the property, the neighborhood, the sale price, and a short note about what made the transaction notable, like a fast close or a tricky negotiation. The app should feel tasteful and confident, the kind of thing a buyer or seller would find genuinely reassuring.

Make a biomedical researcher publication app for mobile that feels like a proper home for serious work — something that treats the papers and findings with the gravity they deserve rather than reducing them to a plain scrollable list. Each publication should be presented with the journal name, year, a plain-language summary of what the research found, and a link to read more. The app should feel precise and clean, the kind of digital presence that actually reflects the intellectual weight of the work.

Make a ceramics artist workshop showcase app for my phone that has the same handmade quality as the work itself — earthy, tactile, genuinely warm. The app should open to a gallery of finished pieces grouped loosely by collection or firing technique, with each piece showing a close-up photo and a note about the clay, the process, and what inspired the form. There should also be a small section about upcoming workshops so people can actually come learn. The whole thing should feel like it belongs to a real maker.

Build a financial planner success stories app for mobile that actually earns the trust it's asking for — something that feels honest and human rather than polished and hollow. Each story should lead with the client situation in real terms, describe the plan that was put in place, and show the outcome clearly with a concrete number or milestone. The app should feel like it has real conviction behind it, the kind of portfolio a prospective client opens on their phone and feels genuinely moved by.

Build a forensic science analyst profile app for mobile that feels as precise and serious as the field itself — nothing flashy, just the kind of clean, confident presentation that says this person knows exactly what they're doing. The app should open with a short professional summary and then move into areas of specialization, notable case contributions described in general terms, and published findings or certifications. The feel should be authoritative without being cold — credible, focused, and built with intention.

Make a photography portfolio app for my phone that feels like the photographer actually had a say in how their work is presented — not just a grid that could belong to anyone, but something with a distinct visual voice and a sense of occasion. The app should open with a full-bleed featured shot and then let you browse work by series or subject, with each photo given enough room to breathe. Tapping a photo should bring up a short note about where it was taken and what the photographer was going after.

Create a UI/UX designer case studies app for mobile that actually reflects the craft — something where the presentation itself is part of the argument, showing that this person thinks carefully about how things feel and flow. Each case study should walk through the problem, the thinking behind the design decisions, and the final result with a few key screens shown clearly. The home screen of the app should make it easy to browse by industry or project type so the right work surfaces quickly for the right audience.

Need a graphic designer brand book app for mobile that feels like it has the same level of care and intention as the work it's showcasing — something that understands its own visual identity and holds it consistently from the first tap to the last. Each brand project should show the final logo and palette alongside a short story about what the client needed and the thinking that shaped the direction. The app should feel like a statement piece — the kind of portfolio that announces a clear point of view.

Build a resume and CV builder app for my phone that actually has taste — not a fill-in-the-blank form that spits out the same template everyone else uses, but something that helps you put together a CV that feels genuinely yours. The app should guide you through the key sections like experience, education, and skills, let you choose from a small set of layouts that each have their own personality, and show a live preview as you fill things in. The result should feel crafted, not generated.

Need a mobile app for an illustrator's artwork gallery that feels like the artist's own handpicked space — something with a sense of identity and editorial intention rather than just dumping every piece into a grid and calling it done. The app should let you browse work by theme or medium, with each piece given a title, a short note about what it was made for, and enough visual room to actually appreciate it. The whole thing should feel like stepping into a studio, not scrolling a stock site.

Need a freelance copywriter samples app for mobile that feels like the writer actually thought about how their work should live on a phone — something with a reading-forward design that makes the copy itself the star, not the packaging. The app should organize samples by type, like brand voice, long-form editorial, and short ads, with each piece showing cleanly with a line about the client and the brief it answered. It should feel like a confident, considered statement of how this person works.

An architect project portfolio app for mobile that carries the weight and intention of the built work — something that treats each project as its own small world rather than just a thumbnail in a list. The app should present each project with a strong lead image, the program type like residential or cultural, the location, and a short statement about the design idea at the center of it. Tapping in should reveal more photos and a brief note on what made this project worth doing. It should feel spare and precise, the way good architecture does.

A fashion stylist lookbook app for mobile that has the visual confidence and point of view to actually represent the work — something that feels curated down to the last detail, not assembled. The app should open to a full-bleed editorial image and then let you browse looks organized by client, season, or occasion, with each look showing the full outfit and a short note on the story behind it. The whole thing should feel like a well-made print book that happens to live on your phone.

Make a government services digital brochure app for mobile that actually feels like something a real person designed with care — not the usual bureaucratic wall of text that nobody finishes reading. The app should organize services clearly by category, like permits, benefits, and public records, with each one having a plain-language description of what it is, who it's for, and how to access it. The overall feel should be approachable and trustworthy, the kind of thing that makes dealing with public services feel a little less exhausting.

Create a legal firm case study showcase app for mobile that feels like it was built with the same rigor the firm applies to its actual work — nothing decorative, just a clean and credible presentation that earns trust quickly. Each case should lead with the area of law, the challenge the client faced, the approach the firm took, and the outcome in plain terms. The home screen of the app should make it easy to browse by practice area so the right cases surface for the right visitors without any friction.
